result.text: Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
